newsitem.title: UK: Belarus faces rough ride at European summit.
newsitem.headline: Belarus faces rough ride at European summit.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko of Belarus can expect a rough ride from European nations at a security summit next week, with protests expected over his autocratic rule and attempts to secure more powers.
Diplomats said Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, whose country currently holds the European Union presidency, may meet Lukashenko at the summit in Lisbon to express the EU's displeasure and concern.
"A number of countries will have things to say about what has been going on, that much is clear, and it will not be comfortable for Lukashenko," said another Western diplomat.

The EU said earlier this week it was seriously concerned about events in Belarus, a former Soviet republic of 10 million people which occupies an important strategic position between Russia and Eastern Europe.

Lukashenko has been trying to shut down the parliament following his resounding victory in a controversial referendum last weekend, which has been condemned by Western nations as an unconstitutional grab for power.
Leaders from the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) meet in Lisbon next week and Lukashenko has said he will attend.
OSCE Secretary-General Giancarlo Aragona is in Belarus this week to voice the organisation's concerns.

The forum could vote to suspend Belarussian membership if all others members agree, as happened with Yugoslavia in 1992. But diplomats said this was not a likely option because many nations wanted to try first to resolve the problem through dialogue.
The country's neighbours -- Russia, Ukraine, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland -- have all expressed concern over the crisis.
